topics.name: Supply and Demand
topics.summary: Supply and demand determine market equilibrium price and quantity.

topics.name: Price Elasticity of Demand
topics.summary: Price elasticity of demand measures how responsive quantity demanded is to changes in price.

topics.name: Price Controls
topics.summary: Binding price ceilings can create shortages, while binding price floors can create surpluses.

questions.question: If demand increases while supply remains unchanged, what happens to equilibrium price and quantity?
questions.explanation: A rightward demand shift increases both equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity, assuming an upward-sloping supply curve.

questions.question: If the absolute value of price elasticity of demand is greater than 1, demand is:
questions.explanation: Demand is elastic when the absolute value of price elasticity of demand exceeds 1.

questions.question: What is the typical effect of a binding price ceiling in a competitive market?
options: A guaranteed increase in producer surplus
questions.explanation: A binding price ceiling is below equilibrium, causing quantity demanded to exceed quantity supplied.

questions.question: With a downward-sloping demand curve, what does a rise in the good’s own price cause, holding other demand determinants fixed?
options: A decrease in quantity demanded along the demand curve
questions.explanation: A change in the good’s own price causes movement along its demand curve rather than a shift of the curve.

questions.question: For a normal good, what happens to demand when consumer income rises, all else equal?
questions.explanation: A normal good is one whose demand increases as income rises.

questions.question: What happens to the supply curve when production costs fall, all else equal?
options: There is only a movement along supply
questions.explanation: Lower production costs let producers supply more at each price, shifting supply right.

questions.question: With downward-sloping demand and upward-sloping supply, what follows from an increase in supply alone?
options: Lower equilibrium price and higher equilibrium quantity
questions.explanation: A rightward supply shift lowers the intersection price and raises the intersection quantity.

questions.question: What is market equilibrium?
options: A situation where all buyers get unlimited goods
A price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, planned purchases and sales match, so there is no shortage or surplus at that price.

questions.question: If quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price, what is present?
options: A decrease in demand by definition
questions.explanation: A shortage is excess demand: buyers want more than sellers offer at the current price.

questions.question: Tea and coffee are substitutes. If the price of coffee rises, what happens to demand for tea, all else equal?
questions.explanation: Some buyers switch from coffee to tea, increasing tea demand.

questions.question: Cars and gasoline are complements. If gasoline becomes more expensive, what happens to demand for cars, all else equal?
questions.explanation: A higher cost of using cars reduces demand for cars when the goods are complements.

questions.question: If Qd = 20 − 2P and Qs = 2P, what is the equilibrium price?
questions.explanation: Set 20 − 2P = 2P, giving 4P = 20 and P = 5; equilibrium quantity is 10.

questions.question: Price rises from 10 to 12 and quantity demanded falls from 100 to 80. What is the absolute midpoint price elasticity, rounded to two decimals?
questions.explanation: The midpoint quantity change is −20/90 and the midpoint price change is 2/11. The absolute ratio is 11/9 ≈ 1.22.

questions.question: What does an absolute price elasticity of demand of 0.4 mean?
questions.explanation: An absolute elasticity below 1 means quantity demanded changes by a smaller percentage than price.

questions.question: If demand is elastic over a price increase, what happens to total revenue?
questions.explanation: With elastic demand, the percentage quantity decline exceeds the percentage price increase, so price times quantity falls.

questions.question: If demand is inelastic over a price increase, what happens to total revenue?
questions.explanation: The percentage quantity decline is smaller than the percentage price increase, so total revenue rises.

questions.question: What shape represents perfectly inelastic demand?
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic demand, quantity demanded does not respond to price changes.

questions.question: Which demand is generally more price elastic, all else equal?
options: Demand for a necessity with no substitutes
Demand for a good with many close substitutes
Demand when buyers have no time to adjust
questions.explanation: Close substitutes make it easier for buyers to switch when a price changes, increasing price responsiveness.

questions.question: What sign of cross-price elasticity indicates substitute goods?
questions.explanation: When the price of one substitute rises, demand for the other rises, producing positive cross-price elasticity.

questions.question: What does negative income elasticity indicate?
questions.explanation: For an inferior good, demand falls as income rises, so income elasticity is negative.

questions.question: At a point with unit-elastic demand, what is the absolute price elasticity?
questions.explanation: Unit elasticity means equal-magnitude percentage changes in price and quantity demanded.

questions.question: Relative to the unregulated equilibrium price, where must a price ceiling be to bind?
options: Above every buyer’s willingness to pay
questions.explanation: A ceiling constrains the market only when it prevents the price from reaching the higher equilibrium level.

questions.question: What is the usual effect of a binding price floor in a competitive market?
options: No change in transactions under any conditions
questions.explanation: A binding floor is above equilibrium, making quantity supplied greater than quantity demanded.

questions.question: A market has equilibrium price 8. What is the effect of a price ceiling of 10?
options: It sets the market price to 10
It is nonbinding and leaves the equilibrium unchanged
questions.explanation: A maximum price above the equilibrium does not restrict the equilibrium trade.

questions.question: A market has equilibrium price 8. What is the effect of a price floor of 6?
options: It is nonbinding and leaves the equilibrium unchanged
It sets the market price to 6
questions.explanation: A minimum price below the equilibrium does not prevent trade at the equilibrium price.

questions.question: At a binding ceiling, Qd = 120 and Qs = 70. How large is the shortage?
questions.explanation: The shortage is quantity demanded minus quantity supplied: 120 − 70 = 50.

questions.question: At a binding floor, Qs = 100 and Qd = 60. How large is the surplus?
questions.explanation: The surplus is quantity supplied minus quantity demanded: 100 − 60 = 40.

questions.question: Under a binding ceiling with Qd = 120 and Qs = 70, how many units can trade if sellers supply exactly Qs and there are no other sources?
questions.explanation: Only 70 units are supplied, so trade cannot exceed 70 even though buyers want 120.

questions.question: In the basic competitive labor-market model, what follows from a minimum wage above equilibrium?
options: Quantity of labor supplied exceeds quantity of labor demanded
Quantity of labor demanded exceeds supply
questions.explanation: A binding wage floor creates excess labor supply in this model; this is a model prediction, not a claim about every real labor market.

questions.question: Why can a binding price control create deadweight loss in the basic competitive model with no externalities?
options: Some mutually beneficial trades no longer occur
The government must buy all output
questions.explanation: When a control reduces trade below the efficient equilibrium quantity, some trades with benefits exceeding costs are lost.
